acs.text: Scenario: Registration creates the customer without echoing the password. Given a new customer with a unique e-mail address, When their details are posted to POST /users/register, Then the API responds 201 with the customer's details and an id, And the response does not contain the password
outcomes: the response contains the customer's details and an id
the response does not contain the password

acs.text: Scenario: A registered e-mail address cannot register twice. Given a customer already registered with an e-mail address, When the same e-mail address is registered again, Then the API responds 409 with the message "A customer with this email address already exists."
outcomes: second registration with the same e-mail address responds 409
message "A customer with this email address already exists."

acs.text: Scenario: Weak passwords are rejected with every broken rule listed. Given a new customer whose password is "abc", When they register, Then the API responds 422 and the password errors state all four rules: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number
outcomes: the password errors state the rule: at least 8 characters
the password errors state the rule: upper and lower case letters
the password errors state the rule: a symbol
the password errors state the rule: a number

acs.text: Scenario: Signing in on the web shop. Given a registered customer on the web shop's sign-in page, When they sign in with their e-mail address and password, Then they land on the "My account" page, And the navigation shows their first and last name
outcomes: after signing in they land on the "My account" page
the navigation shows the customer's first and last name

acs.text: Scenario: A wrong password is refused. Given a registered customer, When they sign in with a wrong password, Then POST /users/login responds 401, And the web shop shows "Invalid email or password"
outcomes: POST /users/login with a wrong password responds 401
the web shop shows "Invalid email or password"

acs.text: Scenario: The account locks after five failed attempts. Given a registered customer, When five sign-in attempts with a wrong password are made, Then attempts one to five respond 401, And the sixth attempt, even with the correct password, responds 423 with a message that the account is locked
outcomes: wrong-password sign-in attempts one to five each respond 401
the sixth attempt, even with the correct password, responds 423
the sixth attempt's response has a message that the account is locked

acs.text: Scenario: Signing out invalidates the token. Given a signed-in customer with an access token, When they sign out with GET /users/logout, Then GET /users/me with the same token responds 401
outcomes: after GET /users/logout, GET /users/me with the same token responds 401

rules.text: Password rules: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number; a registration breaking them is rejected with 422 and every broken rule listed
An e-mail address can be registered only once; a second registration responds 409
The account locks after five failed sign-in attempts: attempts one to five respond 401, the sixth attempt responds 423 even with the correct password
The registration response never contains the password
Signing out invalidates the access token: GET /users/me with that token then responds 401

errorModel.case: registering an e-mail address that is already registered (POST /users/register)
errorModel.body: A customer with this email address already exists.

errorModel.case: registering with a weak password (POST /users/register): password errors state every broken rule
signing in with a wrong password (POST /users/login), including failed attempts one to five
signing in with a wrong password on the web shop: message shown on the sign-in page (UI text, not an API body)
sign-in after five failed attempts, even with the correct password (POST /users/login): message that the account is locked (wording not specified, G6)
GET /users/me with a token that was signed out via GET /users/logout

oracleGaps.value: A rule counts as stated when the 422 response's password errors include a message that names it: the 8-character minimum, upper and lower case letters, a symbol, a number. Exact wording is not checked.
The response contains an id and echoes the submitted details (at least first name, last name and e-mail address) with the values posted.
The 423 response carries a message that says the account is locked (contains the word "locked", case-insensitive); exact wording is not checked.
